events.label: birth
events.text: Sir John Francis Charles de Salis born in 1864.

evidence.quote: ( 19 July 1864 – 14 January 1939 ) was an Anglo-Irish British diplomat and landowner

events.text: Began education at Eton.

evidence.quote: After being educated at Eton ( 1877–1882 , Edward Compton Austen Leighs house )

events.text: Ended education at Eton.

evidence.quote: After being educated at Eton ( 1877–1882 , Edward Compton Austen Leighs house )

events.text: Nominated attaché in the diplomatic service.

evidence.quote: he was nominated an attaché in the diplomatic service on 20 November 1886

events.label: examination
events.text: Passed a competitive diplomatic examination.

evidence.quote: He passed a competitive examination on 14 January 1887

events.text: Appointed attaché at Brussels.

evidence.quote: On 12 June 1888 he was appointed to Brussels as an attaché

events.text: Promoted to Third Secretary.

evidence.quote: promoted to Third Secretary on 14 January 1889

events.text: Married Hélène Marie de Riquet, Comtesse de Caraman-Chimay.

evidence.quote: He married in 1890 Hélène Marie de Riquet

events.text: Began service in Madrid.

evidence.quote: From 24 April 1892 he served in Madrid

events.text: Promoted to Second Secretary.

evidence.quote: promoted to Second Secretary on 22 August 1893

events.text: Began service in Cairo under Lord Cromer.

evidence.quote: From August 1894 he served in Cairo under Lord Cromer

events.label: allowance
events.text: Granted an allowance for knowledge of Arabic.

evidence.quote: he was granted an allowance for knowledge of Arabic on 2 April 1895

events.text: Was in Berlin in autumn.

evidence.quote: In autumn 1897 he was in Berlin

events.text: Was in Brussels.

evidence.quote: in 1899 in Brussels

events.text: Became head of chancery in Athens.

evidence.quote: from 1901 in Athens , as head of chancery ( dealing with the Macedonian problem )

events.text: Began employment at the Foreign Office in London.

evidence.quote: He was employed between 1901–06 at the Foreign Office in London

events.text: His wife Hélène de Riquet died.

evidence.quote: Comtesse de Caraman-Chimay ( 18 August 1864 – 31 May 1902 )

events.text: Promoted to First Secretary.

evidence.quote: He was promoted to First Secretary on 1 April 1904

events.text: Appointed British delegate for Romanian commercial convention negotiation.

evidence.quote: appointed a British Delegate for negotiation of a new Commercial Convention with Romania on 7 September 1905

events.text: Ended employment at the Foreign Office in London.

evidence.quote: He was employed between 1901–06 at the Foreign Office in London

events.text: British delegate at the International Copyright Conference, Berlin.

evidence.quote: a British delegate at the International Copyright Conference at Berlin , October–November 1908

events.text: Ended service as Berlin chargé d'affaires and counsellor of embassy.

events.text: Authored Report on German Finances (Cd. 5465-19).

evidence.quote: J . F . C . De Salis , Report on German Finances , Cd . 5465-19 , 1911

events.text: Began service as Envoy Extraordinary to the King of Montenegro at Cettinjé.

evidence.quote: From November 1911 to 1916 he served as Envoy Extraordinary and Minister Plenipotentiary

events.text: Ended service as Envoy to Montenegro.

evidence.quote: From November 1911 to 1916 he served as Envoy Extraordinary and Minister Plenipotentiary

events.text: Sent by British Government to investigate Serbian occupation of Montenegro.

evidence.quote: In 1919 the British Government sent de Salis to investigate the Serbian occupation of Montenegro
